title: George Lewis and Frank Lewis on clarinet
summary: Clarinetists he watched, especially George Lewis, how he played, and whether Frank Lewis was his father.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Who were some of the other good clarinet players in those days that you used to watch and listen to?

Well, the son of a woman I used to watch, and he used to play so much all the time, left for the other folks I wouldn't be playing. He'd be sitting down, fooling around. That's George Lewis. George Lewis. Bert and Bakke and all of them.
Did you hear the TOs? How were they?

He used to do better than all of them, all of them. To me, I don't know about it but to me. He used to have to work, work with everybody. He used to blow a clarinet. I tried many times practically, but I never could do it. He'd never come out like that, ain't he? Puffy jawed out. He'd never go out like that. He'd never seen him look like he ain't blind.
Never did puff him out then?
No, I'd puff at all. He'd puff from the inside.
Yeah, didn't move his...
From the inside. He'd never go in like that. He'd never go out like that.
Was that Lorenzo TO?
No, George Lewis.
Oh, George Lewis or that Frank Lewis you mean?
Frank Lewis, yeah. Frank Lewis. Frank Lewis. Well, that's two Lewis. I didn't know George was playing back then. And then George Lewis played something like Frank Lewis.
Yeah.

And I used to judge him many times. I said, George, you used to go over at Lake Two. You used to show that when you was little now. I said, I believe George you're a poor boy. He said, I don't know. I said, you're a son. I said, well, that's going to make you ain't nothing in your daddy. I said, man, this is a half children and women and they're gone. You never see them anymore, you know? Yeah, that's right. I believe that's George's daddy too. Lil Frank Lewis was a sharp old guy. You really didn't think he might have been? I didn't think he might have been.
I didn't think he was George's father. Yeah, yeah.
I never did ask him about his father. He don't talk much about it. No, he don't talk about that. Nobody, nobody. No, never said a word about it. I asked him a couple of times.
And his mother, you know, is named Zeno now. Yeah.
I don't know if she was married again.
But he was married again. And then they're gone.
They're gone.
They're gone. They're gone.
They're gone. They're gone. They're gone. They're gone.
They're gone.
They're gone. They're gone.
I don't know if they were married again. I don't know if they were married or what. I ought to ask her sometime. I mean, I wonder if she was any relation to this.
